newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins firm mainly on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins firm mainly on foreign buying.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds firmed on Friday, mainly on foreign buying, and dealers said an upward trend was apparently gaining ground after a two-day decline.
"Prices eased a little in early trading but then the rise started mainly on foreign interest," an ICFI Moscow Partners Bank dealer said.
"People must have realised it is a good time to open new positions after the recent fall," he added.

Another dealer said prices were rising mainly on London bank client buying, though some foreign operators were ready to sell at current prices. He added some local operators are active buyers today as well.
Dealers said the fourth and fifth tranches were traded the most actively. They said prices were likely to firm further in the next few weeks but short-term corrections were highly possible.
"There will be new, higher levels. Other declines are likely, mainly on news about (President Boris) Yeltsin but generally we can look confidently upwards," the ICFI Moscow Partners Bank dealer said.
But another dealer said that next week prices of the fourth and fifth tranches could ease up to one big figure from current levels.
"Yields have achieved certain levels and somebody could push down prices to create positions at lower prices ahead of another rise," he said.
